g.text: Same mechanism as the paper's section 4.2 experiment (there: 0.8 s for a move followed by another move, 1 s otherwise). The gain only

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: appears when AGVs are faster than planned; when everyone is exactly on time both graphs give the same makespan.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Planned waits vs emergent waits when AGVs run early

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: AGV-1 and AGV-2 are lightly loaded and need only 0.5 s per move; everything else takes 1 s, a wait action also 1 s. With

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: waits in the graph, AGV-3 and AGV-4 still sit out their full planned waits. Without them, AGV-3 and AGV-4 wait exactly

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: as long as the dependencies require, and the gain cascades down the convoy.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: A3-2 starts at 2.5 s: AGV-2 left W22 at 2 s, but AGV-3's 1-s wait A3-1 must run out first

g.text: A3-2 starts at 2 s, the moment A2-2 completes
